question: Which feature is commonly found in modern anti-virus software to help with real-time threat detection?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cloud-based detection**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cloud-based detection__ is a technology used in modern antivirus software.
 
• It enables the software to analyze threats in real-time by connecting to a cloud database.
 
• Threat definitions and updates are stored in the cloud, allowing faster detection of new malware.
 
• It reduces the need for frequent manual updates on user devices.
 
• Cloud-based detection ensures better protection against sophisticated and evolving cyber threats.
 
• This feature optimizes system performance by offloading intensive scanning processes to the cloud.
 
• Many modern antivirus solutions now rely on this technology for enhanced security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Manual Updates:**
 
 
• This method requires users to manually download and install updates to keep the antivirus software current.
 
• It is less efficient compared to automated or cloud-based updates.
 
 
 
• **Offline Scanning:**
 
 
• Offline scanning allows antivirus software to scan for threats without an active internet connection.
 
• This method is useful for detecting known threats based on the locally stored virus database.
 
 
 
• **Passive Scanning:**
 
 
• Passive scanning does not actively monitor the system in real-time but instead scans files or devices when initiated by the user.
 
• It is less effective in providing immediate threat detection compared to real-time scanning.
